name: Dev-via-spec Architect Emit → Builder Handoff
description: When the dev-via-spec-architect emits decide(action=tasks_emitted) AND the emit_dev_via_spec_artifact tool has minted the dev_via_spec.artifact.path marker triple on the architect's loop entity, this rule fires and spawns the dev-via-spec-builder. The builder calls bootstrap_workspace as iteration 1 (creates the sandbox worktree at its own loop_id and seeds the rendered spec markdown as SPEC.md), then iterates bash to write code and run tests, terminating with builder_decide. R3.6.2.d of ADR-032 §R3.6.2.

on_enter.subject: agent.task.dev-via-spec-builder
on_enter.prompt:
The dev-via-spec architect has emitted a structured spec artifact. Architect loop id: $entity.instance. Spec path on host filesystem: $entity.triple.dev_via_spec.artifact.path. Spec slug: $entity.triple.dev_via_spec.artifact.slug.

Iteration 1 — call bootstrap_workspace exactly once with the spec_path above:

  bootstrap_workspace(spec_path="$entity.triple.dev_via_spec.artifact.path")

This creates your sandbox worktree at this loop's task_id and seeds the spec markdown as SPEC.md in the workspace root.

Iteration 2 onward — read the spec via `bash cat SPEC.md`, then iterate bash calls (mvn compile, mvn test, etc.) per your 10-bash-iteration-contract.md. Terminate with builder_decide per your 20-builder-decide-contract.md when tests pass, when the iteration budget is exhausted, or when you genuinely cannot proceed without clarification.

metadata.pattern: builder spawn with product-shell bootstrap_workspace tool as iteration-1 setup hook (ADR-032 §addendum 2026-05-03 R3.6.2.d records why this is product-local instead of an http_request rule action)
metadata.ordering_invariant: This rule trusts the architect's emit-then-decide ordering: emit_dev_via_spec_artifact publishes the dev_via_spec.artifact.{path,slug,...} triples BEFORE decide(action=tasks_emitted) publishes the coordinator.next_action triple. Consequently when this rule fires on coordinator.next_action=tasks_emitted, the artifact triples are already on the entity and $entity.triple.dev_via_spec.artifact.path resolves. If the architect persona is ever reordered to call decide first, the rule's prompt substitution will produce an empty path and bootstrap_workspace will reject. The properties.spec_path passthrough is the redundant channel — task properties are an independent surface that does not depend on triple-substitution timing. The reviewer's R3.6.2.d notes flagged this as a contract worth pinning here so a future persona refactor doesn't quietly break the chain. Beta.39 does not ship an `exists` operator, so we cannot defensively gate on the path triple's presence; the ordering invariant is the load-bearing assumption.
metadata.spec_handoff_caveat: The bootstrap_workspace tool reads the spec markdown from $SEMTEAMS_DEVVIASPEC_ARTIFACT_DIR (default docs/specs) on the backend host. The sandbox container must be able to reach the backend's filesystem only via the product-shell tool path — bash inside the sandbox cannot read host files directly. Migration: when upstream ships an http_request rule action plus a substitution variable for publish_agent's generated task_id, this rule can do the seed inline and bootstrap_workspace can be deleted.
metadata.terminal_role_note: builder_decide(action=tests_passing|tests_failing|needs_clarification) is terminal. No rule fires on those actions today. R3.5's coordinator-as-meta-reviewer rule may add routing on needs_clarification (ADR-031 §addendum 2026-05-02). For now operators read the terminal verdict from the loop trajectory.
